Management Discussion and Analysis Year 2017              
 
                              1  
Key events in 2017 
 
 
March 16, 2017:  The Bank redeemed the Subordinated Debentures No. 1/2012 Due 2022, with the 
Issuer’s Early Redemption Right in the whole amount of Baht 5,155.00 million. 
August 1, 2017:  Mr.Supant Mongkolsuthree resigned from Bank’s Independent director. 
November 2, 2017:  The Bank redeemed the Subordinated Debentures No. 2/2012 Due 2022, with the 
Issuer’s Early Redemption Right  in the whole amount of Baht 15,133.32 million. 
Moreover, in the same month,  the Bank issued Thai baht -denominated Basel III – 
compliant Tier2 subordinated unsecured debenture amounted to Baht 20,000 
million. 
November 24, 2017:  Mr.Vichai Assarasakorn  was appointed to be Bank’s Director and Independent 
Director in place of Mr.Supant Mongkolsuthree who resigned.

Management Discussion and Analysis Year 2017              
 
                              2  
Management Discussion and Analysis for the year 2017 
 
This report discusses the principal changes in the audited consolidated financial statem ents for the year ended 
December 31, 2017. In June 2017, the Bank has combined National ITMX Co., Ltd to the Bank’s associate 
company in accordance with Thai Accounting Standard 28 (TAS 28): Investments in Associates and Joint 
Ventures. The Bank considered  its shareholding together with its power to participate in the company’s 
operating policy through its representatives in the position of the company’s board of directors as significant 
influence to the company. The Bank also restated the consolidated fina ncial statements for Statements of 
Financial Position as at December 31, 2016 and Statements of Comprehensive Income for the year ended 
December 31, 2016. However, the above change had insignificant impact to financial position and performance 
of the Bank. 
 
The Bank and Its Subsidiaries’ Overview for the year 2017 
In 2017, the Thai economy continued to expand due mainly to expor ts and tourism sectors.  Merchandise 
exports continued to grow in all major export destinations and most product categories. Meanwhile, the tourism 
sector expanded significantly due to increased foreign tourists especially Chinese and ASEAN tourists. 
However, the growth in the pr ivate investment sector remained relatively low and concentrated only in a few 
business sectors. In addition, the expansion of private consumption was suppressed by the decreased in farm 
income during the second half of the year and the high household debt  problem, which lowered purchasing 
power of low-income households. 
 
For the year 2017, KTB’s consolidated pre -provision profit was Baht 73,741 million, decreased by Baht 316 
million (0.43%). Fee and service income and operating expenses improved and offset  the slight decrease in net 
interest income. In summary, the key changes of the Bank and its subsidiaries’ financial result compared to last 
year are as shown below: 
1) Net interest income declined by Baht 1,188 million (1.37%) due mainly to the impact of the lending rate 
cut on Minimum Retail Rate (MRR) at 0.50% in mid of May 2017. Despite the mentioned impact on yield, the 
Bank has continued to actively manage funding cost, resulting in the slight decrease on Net Interest Margin 
(NIM) by 0.06% to 3.24%, compared to 3.30% at the year 2016. 
2) Net fee and service income increased by Baht 1,979 million (8.98%) as a result of the expansion of fee 
from ATM card business, electronic banking service fees and Bancassurance. Meanwhile, KTB’s consolidated 
total othe r operating income decreased by Baht 2,342 million (14.94%) from the year 2016 because of the 
lessening of net gain on trading and foreign exchange transactions as well as the decelerating of share of profit 
from investments on equity method from the Bank’ s associated company from insurance sector.  The Bank had 
revenues from litigation settlement amounted to Baht 1,636 million.  
3) Other operating expenses reduced by Baht 1,235 million (2.44%) as the Bank continues its cost 
management policy resulting in the  slight reduction of the cost-to-income ratio compared to  last year, from 
40.61% to 40.11%. 
4) The Bank and its subsidiaries continue to maintain a prudent coverage ratio. As at the end of 
December 2017, coverage ratio was 121.71%. Provision expenses incre ased by Baht 11,404 million (34.11%) 
from 2016, partly due to the preparation to comply with the International Financial Reporting Standard 9: IFRS9. 
 
In 2017, The Bank and its subsid iaries’ net profit was Baht 24,110 million, showing a decline of Baht 9,455 
million (28.17%) and the Net Profit Attributable to Equity Holders of the Bank was Baht 22,440 million, 
decreased by Baht 9,864 million (30.53%), mainly due to the increase of provision expense. 
 
The Bank’s consolidated total loan to customers (less  deferred revenue) was Baht 1,938,082 million, rose by 
Baht 33,993 million (1.79%) from year 2016. The Bank focused on quality of loan growth as the loans to 
government and state enterprise sector were well expanded. The Bank’s consolidated deposits increa sed by

Baht 98,471 million (4.99%) from saving s and demand deposits while time deposits decreased as the Bank’s 
funding cost management policy and brought about loans to customers (less deferred revenue) -to-deposits 
ratio at 93.59%. 
 
The Bank’ consolidated NPLs as at December 31, 2017 was Baht 103,020 million, and gross NPLs ratio was 
4.19% rose from 3.97% as at December 31, 2016. The Bank has continued to improve its strategies and 
business operating process emphasizing on quality of loan portfolio along with enhancing efficiency of 
monitoring and restructuring process. The Bank will maintain its coverage ratio at the appropriate level.  
 
Overall, the Bank and its subsidiaries have strong financial position, solid capital level and effe ctive business 
operation to cope with any uncertainty in the future.

funding cost, resulting in the slight decrease on Net Interest Margin (NIM) by 0.0 6% to 3.24%, compared to 
3.30% at the year 2016.

Impairment Loss of Loans and Debt Securities 
 
In 2017, the Bank and its subsidiaries set aside provision for impairment loss of loans and debt securities 
amounted to Baht 44,833 million, increased by Baht 11,404 million (34.11%) compared to the year 2016. The 
bank set aside more provision to be a buff er for the increased NPLs, maintain its coverage ratio and prepare to 
comply with the International Financial Reporting Standard 9: IFRS9 . Thus, the Banks and its subsidiaries’ 
coverage ratio was 121.71% slightly changed from 121.57% as at December 31, 201 6 and also increased from 
115.37% as at September 30, 2017. 
 
In 2017 and 2016, the Banks wrote off NPLs in amount of Baht 23,739 million and Baht 1,509 million 
respectively.

Liabilities 
 
The Bank’s consolidated deposits as at December 31, 2017 were Baht 2,070,875 million, enlarged by Baht 
98,471 million (4.99%) from December 31, 2016 due to the growth of savings and demand deposits, despite 
some contraction of time deposits. The Bank’s consolidated loans to customers (less deferred revenue) -to-
deposits ratio was 93.59%, decreased from the end of the yea r 2016 at 96.54%. Meanwhile, the net interbank 
and money market items were Baht 228,691 million; increased by Baht 17,520 million (8.30%), boosting up the 
Bank’s consolidated total liabilities by Baht 149,692 million (6.21%) to Baht 2,559,991 million. 
 
In March and November 2017, the Bank redeemed t he sets of Thai Baht subordinated debentures in full, 
amounted to Baht 5,155 million and Baht 15,133 million respectively and also issued a set of Thai Baht 
subordinated debenture as the replacement, amounted to Baht 20,000 million in November 2017. 
 
 Deposits classified by types 
 
 
Equity 
 
The total equity (Equity holders of the Bank) as at December 31, 2017 amounted to Baht 287,861 million, 
showing an increase of Baht 13,674 million (4.99%) from December 31, 2016. 
 
Book value per share (Equity holders of the Bank) was Baht 20.59 per share, increased from Baht 19.61 per 
share at the end of the year 2016. 
 
Sources and Uses of Funds 
 
As at December 31, 2017, 72. 56% of the Bank’s source of funds was deposits; the rests were interbank 
borrowings, debt issued and borrowings, and equity. The Bank’s use of funds comprised of 67. 90% loans to 
customers (less deferred revenue), 19.26% net interbank and money market items, and 8.00% net investments 
and net investments in subsidiaries and associates.

Statutory Capital Fund 
 
As of December 31, 2017, the Bank and the Financial Business Group Common Equity Tier 1 was Baht 
267,456 million (13.42% of its Risk -weighted assets (RWA)). The Tier I capital was Baht 268,606 million 
(13.48% of its RWA). Total capital was Baht 342,748 million (17.20% of its RWA), increased from 16.60% as at 
December 31, 2016. The increase of capital ratio was due to the appropriation of its net profit for the first half of 
2017 for capital. 
 
In 2017 the Bank issued its subordinated debentures, as Tier 2 capital, of Baht 20,000 million to replace the 
redeemed debentures of Baht 20,288 million. 
 
Currently, the bank possesses healthy capital ratios compared to BOT’s requirement. Moreove r, the bank 
regularly reassesses the capital level to be in accordance with the BOT’s requirement as well as any 
foreseeable risk to ensure the adequate capital.

Asset Quality 
 
Non-Performing Loans 
 
The Bank’s consolidated NPLs as at December 31, 2017 was Baht 103,020 million, rose by Baht 11,892 million 
(13.05%) from December 31, 2016 as a consequence of the increase of NPLs from one large corporate client 
group. The gross NPLs ratio was 4.19% increased from 3.97% as at December 31, 2016. However, NPLs 
decreased by Baht 689 million (0.66%) compared to NPLs as at September 30, 2017 
 
In 2017, The Bank improved its strategies and business operating process emphasizing on quality of loan 
portfolio along with enhancing efficiency of monitoring and restructuring process as well as remaining the 
healthy coverage ratio.
